G4630.name: Sceva
G4630.desc: Priest living at the time of the New Testament
G4630.brief: Jewish chief priest whose seven sons attempted to exorcise demons
G4630.short: Sceva was a Jewish chief priest whose seven sons attempted to exorcise demons in the name of Jesus, as mentioned in the book of Acts.

G4658.name: Scythians
G4658.brief: Nomadic people group mentioned by Paul
G4658.short: The Scythians were a nomadic people group known for their barbaric reputation.

G4609.name: Silas
G4609.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G4609.brief: Prominent member of the Jerusalem church, companion of Paul.
G4609.short: Silas (or Silvanus) was a prominent member of the Jerusalem church who accompanied Paul on his second missionary journey and co-wrote some of his epistles.
G4609.meaning: short form of Silvanus, “of the forest” (Latin)

G4613N.name: Simon
G4613N.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G4613N.brief: A tanner in Joppa who hosted Peter.
G4613N.short: Simon was a tanner in Joppa who hosted the apostle Peter in his home.

G4613M.name: Simon
G4613M.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G4613M.brief: Sorcerer in Samaria who tried to buy the Holy Spirit's power.
G4613M.short: Simon was a sorcerer in Samaria who believed and was baptized but later tried to buy the power of the Holy Spirit from the apostles.

G4613L.name: Simon
G4613L.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G4613L.brief: Father of Judas Iscariot, the disciple who betrayed Jesus.
G4613L.short: Simon was the father of Judas Iscariot, the disciple who betrayed Jesus.

G4613G.name: Simon
G4613G.desc: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
G4613G.brief: One of the twelve apostles, also called the Zealot.
G4613G.short: Simon, also known as the Zealot, was one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.

G4613H.name: Simon
G4613H.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G4613H.brief: Brother of Jesus, son of Mary and Joseph.
G4613H.short: Simon was one of the brothers of Jesus, a son of Mary and Joseph.

G4613I.name: Simon
G4613I.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G4613I.brief: A man in Bethany who hosted Jesus for a meal.
G4613I.short: Simon the leper was a man in Bethany who hosted a meal for Jesus, during which a woman anointed Jesus with expensive perfume.

G4613J.name: Simon
G4613J.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G4613J.brief: A man who carried Jesus' cross on the way to crucifixion.
G4613J.short: Simon of Cyrene was compelled by Roman soldiers to carry Jesus' cross on the way to his crucifixion.

G4677.name: Susanna
G4677.desc: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
G4677.brief: Woman who helped support Jesus and his disciples
G4677.short: Susanna was one of the women who provided for Jesus out of her resources.

G4667.name: Smyrna
G4667.brief: One of the seven churches of Asia Minor
G4667.short: Smyrna was one of the seven churches of Asia Minor addressed in the Book of Revelation, known for its persecution and poverty, yet faithful to Christ (<ref="Rev. 1:11; 2:8-11">Rev. 1:11; 2:8-11</ref>).

G4672H.name: Solomon's Portico
G4672H.brief: Colonnade in Jerusalem's temple where apostles taught
G4672H.short: Solomon's Portico, a colonnade in the Jerusalem temple where the apostles gathered to teach (<ref="Act.3.11; 5:12">Act.3.11; 5:12</ref>).

G4681.name: Spain
G4681.brief: Country Paul intended to visit to preach gospel
G4681.short: Spain, a country Paul planned to visit to preach the gospel (<ref="Rom. 15:24, 28">Rom. 15:24, 28</ref>).

G4634.name: Booths Festival
G4634.brief: Jewish festival commemorating the Israelites' wilderness wanderings
G4634.short: The Booths_Festival, also known as the Feast of Tabernacles or Sukkot, was a Jewish festival commemorating the Israelites' wilderness wanderings and God's provision (<ref="Jhn.7.2">Jhn.7.2</ref>).
